determination.question: research why our A/R over 90 has been climbing and what it will take to bring it down
determination.statement: Every figure in this study is measured on your own data. The background notes shaped which readings were taken and never what any number says. The problem is book-wide rather than the work of one or two payers — over-90 share runs from 37.6% at Ashvale Health Plan to 51.6% at Atlas Commercial, with Federal Medicare at 46.9% and Lakewood Medicaid MCO at 49.2% (F1) — and it is equally flat across service lines, where over-120 share spans only 38.8% at Behavioral Health to 43.0% at Emergency (F7). Denied dollars are a small part of that aged exposure — $107,003 of denied A/R sits at 120-plus days, against $972,607 at 31-60 days (F4) — so the aged inventory is overwhelmingly claims waiting or never billed, not claims standing denied. Bringing it down takes clearing the unbilled inventory before the filing clock runs out and staffing the denial queue, in that order. On the denial side, between 62.7% at Summit Peak Medicare Advantage and 74.5% at State Medicaid MCO of denials have never been touched (F6). Institutional claims take about 13 days to reach the payer against about 6 for professional claims in every month measured (F9), so shortening that lag removes a week of age from every institutional claim at the source. 1 reading here measure a rate over a counted population, across 5,113 records the payer has already answered. 12 groups carry a measurement. Everything above is as the data stood on Aug 2, 2026.
